source.title: Dynamical mean-field theory for stochastic gradient descent in Gaussian mixture classification
source.authors: Francesca Mignacco; Florent Krzakala; Pierfrancesco Urbani; Lenka Zdeborov'a

record.tranche_reason: Analyzes random-initialized gradient training and reports training accuracy on synthetic Gaussian-mixture classification problems, a different model and setting from the claim's listed benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy outcomes for two- and three-cluster models. Its CIFAR, depth, initialization-comparison, learning-rate, normalization, and width conditions are not tested. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures training accuracy and generalization in single-layer linear or door-activation classifiers on Gaussian mixtures. These results do not test V1's convolutional networks on CIFAR or the mechanisms and architectures specified by V2–V6. Initialization variance affects generalization here, but activation-matched initialization, signal propagation and trainable depth are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: DMFT tracks the studied high-dimensional learning dynamics, and finite batch size can improve test error through an effective regularizing influence. These conclusions concern Gaussian-mixture classifiers, not the claim's convolutional-network benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes single-layer classifiers on synthetic Gaussian mixtures using a dynamical mean-field framework; it does not reproduce the benchmark experiments in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, regularization, initialization variance, and persistence time affect the reported learning or generalization dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Persistent SGD reaches 100% training accuracy in some parameter regions of the two-cluster Gaussian-mixture problem while generalization error remains positive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly initialized single-layer classifiers can interpolate structured Gaussian-mixture training data under persistent SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing initialization variance affects early-stopping generalization error; in the two-cluster model, the tested initializations approach the same long-time generalization error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale affects transient generalization in single-layer Gaussian-mixture classifiers.

record.problems: Synthetic, high-dimensional Gaussian-mixture task rather than CIFAR benchmarks; training-accuracy outcomes are mostly presented in figures without text description; no comparison against smaller models or corrupted/random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. Training-accuracy outcomes shown only in figures without a corresponding textual description are retained with cannot_determine states; the paper's text-stated 100% training-accuracy finding is represented in R1. Generalization-error, weight-norm, and theory-versus-simulation results were left out because they do not measure the training classification error named by the versions.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels, and comparisons involving model size, early stopping or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious-minimum frequency and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts and special initialization of deep plain or residual networks.
Activation-matched initialization, vanishing or exploding signals and gradients, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, edge of stability and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure text preserves captions and axes but does not permit reliable reconstruction of the plotted training-accuracy outcomes. Failure to read those outcomes is not evidence of absent training success.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random-initialized gradient training and training accuracy in synthetic Gaussian-mixture models, but not the claimed CIFAR benchmarks, corrupted or random labels, or smaller-model and regularized comparisons.
